History:
- 38-year-old woman with 3-day history of profuse diarrhoea (initially watery, now very loose; ≥4 episodes today, “lost count”) and repeated vomiting (last episode ~2 h ago after breakfast); unable to retain food, water, or ORS.
- Subjective high fever (“boiling”); no thermometer measurement.
- Periumbilical abdominal pain/tenderness that comes in waves and triggers urge to defecate.
- No blood noted in stool or urine; urine output present (last void 1 h ago, colour not observed).
- No rash, no prior similar GI episodes.
- Brother and multiple school contacts with similar illness; no recent travel.
- Self-care: oral rehydration solution (salt-sugar mix) 3× day for 2 days without improvement.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic illnesses: none reported.
- Surgical history: none.
- Allergies: not recorded.
- Medications: vitamin D daily (dose/route/frequency not documented); occasional ibuprofen for dysmenorrhoea (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Social: non-smoker, occasional alcohol, no recreational drugs; lives with brother and mother; works as graphic designer.
- Gyn: Last menstrual period 2 weeks ago; not sexually active; no contraception.

Physical Examination:
- Remote consultation; vitals not recorded.
- General: alert and conversing; reports feeling febrile.
- Abdomen: reports marked tenderness around umbilicus.
- Skin: no rash.
- Hydration: able to pass urine within last hour.
- Other systems: not recorded.

Impression:
- Acute infectious gastroenteritis, likely viral (norovirus) given household cluster and abrupt onset.
  • DDx 1: Acute viral gastroenteritis – high likelihood.
  • DDx 2: Acute bacterial gastroenteritis – consider as symptoms persist >72 h; stool culture planned.

Management Plan:
- Arrange urgent in-clinic appointment today for:
  • Assessment of hydration status.
  • Collection of stool sample for microbiological culture.
- Advise continued use of oral rehydration salts: very small, frequent sips.
- Dietary advice: bland/simple foods (toast, biscuits); avoid fruit, vegetables, dairy until settled.
- Red-flag advice: attend A&E (ED) immediately for worsening vomiting, inability to keep down fluids, reduced urine output, high fever, bloody stool, or severe abdominal pain.
- Support line contact given for appointment scheduling and interim concerns.

Patient Summary:
Barbara, 38, presents with 3-day severe diarrhoea, vomiting, periumbilical pain, and subjective fever after exposure to brother with similar illness. Infectious gastroenteritis presumed; stool testing and hydration assessment arranged.

Key Takeaways:
- Keep sipping ORS continually to prevent dehydration.
- Eat only very light foods; avoid produce and dairy for now.
- Seek urgent care if symptoms worsen or you cannot pass urine.

Next Steps:
- Attend same-day clinic visit; submit stool sample.
- Follow up on stool culture results; initiate targeted therapy if bacterial pathogen identified.
- Telephone review or clinic follow-up in 48–72 h to ensure improvement.

● Transcript/DDx conflicts: none noted.
